One man = $2.6 trillion

Seven weeks of falling wiped about $2.6 trillion off Nvidia. Same chips. Same engineers. Same orders. The only thing that changed was one name: Jensen Huang was out. CNBC

Then the board voted him back in, and the stock jumped 31.5% in a single day. admiralmarkets

Everyone is calling this a weakness. I think it's the opposite.

Great companies are not org charts. They are their founders. Apple was Jobs. Tesla is Musk. Nvidia is Huang. The market doesn't pay for GPUs; it pays for the person who decided ten years ago that GPUs would run the world.

Yes, it makes the company fragile. That's the price. A company that survives anyone leaving is usually a company nobody is excited about.

As a developer I take one thing from this: your name is part of your product. People don't follow code, they follow whoever stands behind it. That's why I build under my own.

What do you think: strength or risk?
